title: Self-Exploration
status: draft: written 18 Nov 2026 offline for Grade 7 Social Studies; not yet checked by a CBC Social Studies teacher; not loaded by the live tutor
notes: Keep this personal and safe: learners describe strengths in pairs, never compare or rank. A feelings chart helps learners name emotions before managing them.

skills.key_step: The child tells an ability, a talent, an interest and a skill apart and picks ways to grow them.

floor.prerequisite: Names values in a school situation.
floor.question: A learner hands in lost money. Which value is this?

representations: a strengths card each learner fills in
steps: Ask: born with it, learnt, liked or able to do?
Name it: talent, skill, interest or ability.
Pick a way to grow it.
contexts: a learner who learnt to sew
a quiet learner who listens well

board.say: Typing learnt after practice goes where?

misconceptions.ask: Which of these is an ability?
misconceptions.repair: Ask the child to name three things a classmate does well that are not on stage.

misconceptions.ask: Amina likes football but has not played much. What is football for her?
misconceptions.repair: Ask: can you like something you cannot yet do well?

listen_for: No, you are born good or bad at it
misconceptions.ask: Wanjiku finds drawing hard. Can she get better at it?
misconceptions.repair: Show early and later drawings by the same learner after practice.

misconceptions.ask: Otieno learnt to type fast after months of practice. Is typing a talent or a skill for him?
misconceptions.repair: Sort: born with it (talent), learnt by practice (skill).

checks.question: Amina likes music but cannot yet play an instrument. What is music for her?
Give one way to grow an ability.
checks.answer: any of: practice, feedback, joining a club, a mentor

skills.key_step: The child chooses personal values that make a steady personality and keeps them under pressure.

floor.question: What is an interest?
floor.answer: what a person likes to do

representations: a role play of saying no
steps: Say what a steady person does.
contexts: friends daring a learner to copy
keeping a promise to help at home

board.do: Write: "Friends dare Kevin to skip class."

board.say: Which value helps Kevin say no?

board.do: Write the words Kevin could use.

misconceptions.repair: Ask the child what a person does when they find a lost wallet.

misconceptions.ask: Friends dare Kevin to copy in a test. What does a steady person do?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to trust if Kevin copies once.

misconceptions.ask: Is honesty only a school rule?
misconceptions.repair: Ask whether you would tell the truth at home where the school rules do not apply.

misconceptions.ask: Juma learns he was wrong about a friend. What does a steady person do?
misconceptions.repair: Compare: changing values to please friends, and changing a mistaken idea.

checks.question: Which is a personal value: honesty or a bicycle?
Friends pressure you to do wrong. What does a steady person do?
checks.answer: says no and keeps their values

skills.key_step: The child names feelings and picks healthy ways to manage them over harmful ones.

floor.prerequisite: Labels emotions in self and others.
floor.question: A learner is crying after losing a book. What feeling is this?

misconceptions.ask: What is the best thing to do with anger?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what Wanjiru does when she feels angry at a friend.

misconceptions.ask: Kamau is angry because a friend broke his pencil. What should he do?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what happens to the friendship after the pencil is broken.

misconceptions.ask: Achieng feels sad for many days. What is a healthy step?
misconceptions.repair: Discuss who learners can talk to at school.

misconceptions.ask: How can fear help a person?
misconceptions.repair: Ask what fear makes you do when a dog growls.

checks.question: Give a healthy way to manage anger.
checks.answer: any of: breathe slowly, pause before speaking, talk to a trusted adult, exercise, write it down

checks.question: Is hitting back a healthy way to manage anger?
